context: Riku-teen helps Sho-young memorize multiplication tables.
purpose: Older teen tutoring younger child math.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 陸くん、数学、九九、覚えられない!
lines.en: Riku, I can't memorize my multiplication tables!
lines.style: Urgent, slightly strained whisper-shout. Opens with a little catch in the voice. Quiet intensity — frustration without sulking. Stays grounded, looking for help.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: 繰り返しが大事、毎日やろ。
lines.en: Repetition's the thing. Let's do it every day.
lines.style: Calm, unhurried. Opens soft. Steady rhythm — no urgency in the tone, just quiet certainty. Leans slightly forward, the voice of someone who's done hard things before.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 間違い、ようけしてしまう。
lines.en: I make so many mistakes though.
lines.style: Small voice, hurt underneath. Hesitant attack on the opening word. Breath catching slightly. Not crying yet, but close — the kind of admission that costs something small.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: 計算、ゆっくりで、ええで。
lines.en: Slow math is still good math.
lines.style: Warm reassurance. Soft emphasis on 'slow' — turning it from shame into permission. Gentle but not coddling. The tone of someone older defending the younger one's pace.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: When I get it right, I feel so happy!
lines.style: Sudden brightness. Sharp, genuine smile in the voice. Energetic without being performed. The natural excitement of a child who just remembered why this matters.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: 練習、確実、覚えられるで。
lines.en: With practice, you'll get it. For sure.
lines.style: Quiet conviction. Small pause before the second sentence — a beat that lands like a promise. Warm, steady. The kind of certainty that's earned, not given.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: Thank you. I'm going to try.
lines.style: Soft, determined. Opens with gratitude — genuine relief. Closes with a small tighten in the jaw, like resolve settling in. No performance. Just a child who's decided.
